app.title: DeepMReye: decode gaze from fMRI with a pretrained model (Streamlit app)
app.summary: The person uploads a head-motion-corrected 4D NIfTI fMRI file and picks one of several pretrained models, each trained on a different kind of eye-movement dataset. The app downloads the model weights if they are missing, registers the run to an eye template and pulls out the eyeball voxels. It then shows a quality-control report of the registration and the eye-mask signal. Next it normalises the voxels and runs the network to predict gaze. The predicted X/Y gaze coordinates and an uncertainty value appear in two tables, one row per volume or ten rows per volume, and each table can be downloaded as a CSV.

task.text: Reconstruct where a participant was looking during an fMRI run from the MR signal of the eyeballs, using a pretrained network, and export the gaze coordinates.

data.text: A 4D functional MRI run (3D volumes over time), cut down to eyeball voxels and turned into a table of predicted gaze positions with uncertainty per time point
data.item: a functional volume (one TR) of a motion-corrected fMRI run, with its predicted gaze position

stage.text: decoding gaze from preprocessed fMRI runs, before analysing eye movements alongside brain activity

mechanism.text: A file input and a model dropdown start a fixed pipeline: registration, eye masking, normalisation and inference, with spinners for each step. The pipeline ends in an embedded QC report of slices, a histogram and timecourses, then tabbed tables of per-TR and sub-TR gaze predictions with CSV downloads.

field.text: MR-based eye tracking with deep learning in fMRI cognitive neuroscience

workflow.name: run a pretrained model on an uploaded file and download its predictions

steps.here: A file uploader accepts one head-motion-corrected 4D NIfTI (.nii) run; uploading it starts the pipeline

steps.step: choose which pretrained model to apply
steps.here: A dropdown lists models trained on guided fixations, pursuit, free viewing or combined datasets, with a note on each and a recommended default; missing weights are downloaded
The run is registered to an eye template in MNI space in three passes, and an embedded HTML report shows the eye mask over brain slices, a histogram of eye voxels, and eye vs whole-brain timecourses

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Eye voxels are normalised and passed through the network; per-TR medians of the X/Y gaze and the predicted error are worked out from the sub-TR outputs

steps.step: look over the result at two resolutions
steps.here: Tabs switch between 'Gaze coordinates' (one row per TR) and 'Sub-TR gaze coordinates' (TR × subTR multi-index)
Two download buttons save predicted_gaze_median_<name>.csv and predicted_gaze_subTR_<name>.csv

distinctive: The choice of pretrained model depends on which eye-movement paradigm it was trained on (fixation, pursuit, free viewing), so the person matches the model to their own task
Each prediction carries the network's own uncertainty (predicted Euclidean error) next to the X/Y coordinates
Predictions come at sub-volume resolution, ten per TR, as well as a per-TR median
A spatial registration QC report is shown before results, so a bad eye-mask alignment can be caught
Uploaded data is deleted from the temp folder after each run
